Nugent Commission - SARS

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
SARS has been marred by allegations of corruption and staff exodus recently. Failing to meet its tax collection targets for 3 consecutive years, how will a crippled tax institution impact the taxpayer

Unique Selling Point:
The South African Revenue service is a pivotal institution to the stability of the country. In the past few years as with many other state institutions, SARS has been in the media for all the wrong reasons. From allegations of rogue units to the failure to meet its tax collection targets three years in a row with some of its staff members testifying at the Nugent commission that SARS’ shortfalls are also key to the increase of VAT. How did an institution that is so integral to the welfare of the country get so crippled?

Summary:
When a government institution fails to achieve its core mandate as such with SARS it is a cause for concern. SARS’ main objective is to collect tax revenue for the state, which they have failed to do efficiently for the past three years. The troubles at SARS began with the appointment of Mr Tom Moyane who became SARS commissioner on the 27th of September 2014. Under Mr Moyane’s stewardship the institution has regressed with allegations of corruption, procurement irregularities and staff intimidation from the commissioner himself and his enforcers. This prompted President Cyril Ramaphosa to initiate a commission looking into SARS led by former Judge, Robert Nugent, dubbed the Nugent Commission.

Further information:
Startling testimonies have come out of the commission since it began its work in May 2018 following the suspension of Tom Moyane. For starters a consulting firm, Bain & Company in 2014 conducted a diagnostic for the South African Revenue Service that formed the basis for the overhauling process at the institution and kick-started an entire restructuring process.
To many, the restructuring came as a surprise. It resulted in the closure of crucial arms such as the unit investigating the illicit economy, which chased down the illegal tobacco trade among others, and the Large Business Centre that made sure large enterprises paid their tax dues.
Although Bain & company has pledged to pay back the R164 million they made from SARS for services rendered, the R50b revenue shortfall they have cost SARS in the 2017/18 financial year will take a few years for the institution to recover.

The Nugent commission has also revealed that suspended commissioner Tom Moyane also got involved in dubious appointment of these companies. It appears Moyane met with Bain & co.’s management partner Vittorio Massone at least a year prior to even becoming a commissioner. Massone testified that he had met with Moyane who asked for work to be done on SARS while he was still commissioner of the department correctional services, a clear indication that the two had a relationship before Bain & co got awarded the tender that was only advertised unusually for six days.

Moyane’s iron rule in the institution was not only dominant in the fear entrenched within the SARS staff members who testified at the commission, but his management of SARS also reeked of corruption, similar to that shown in state capture and other state entities.
The appointment of Global advisory firm Gartner and Range wave to have an IT review into SARS was also quite dodgy and had Moyane’s finger prints on it. Patrick Monyeki of Range wave is known to be a close friend of Tom Moyane and he was the one who brought the deal in December 2014 to Gartner, according to the firm’s senior management partner Neville Willemse. Monyeki’s company received 40%, about R80m fro Gartner’s R200m contract with Sars.

Gartener however belives they were not given enough to refute al these allegations by the Nugent commission. They do not know anything about transactions between Patrick Monyeki and SARS or how Gartner was chosen for the contract. According to them, they did not temper with the terms of reference of the job but merely commented on it, which in itself its not illegal, particularly if it will help save costs. An aggrieved Gartner are disappointed by the blame they have received for the collapse of SARS while none of their recommendations were used by SARS.

Judge Dennis Davies who heads up the Davis Tax Committee testified at the Nugent commission that he never saw the need for restructuring at SARS. "Why fix what is to broken" was his comments. Davis was appointed by then finance minister Pravin Gordhan in 2014 to update the process of the Katz commission but instead Commissioner Moyane saw the Davis Tax committee as an enemy. As a result the commission wasn't given access to key data. Furthermore Davis said the recommendations in the Bain report were diametrically opposite to their advice. There were disastrous consequences because of the Large Business Centre Collapse, all kinds of problems in corporate taxes as a result.

David Loxton of Africa forensics and cyber believes that although Judge Nugent has recommended in his report that the President must fire Mr Moyane and appoint a new commissioner, there should be legal repercussions to Mr Moyane and his enforcers at SARS. Corruption is a crime and so those involved must account to the law. David believes there was a concerted effort by Moyane and those close to him to undo all the good within SARS and cripple the institution. This was a corporate strategy to put taxpayer’s monies in risk.

Under Moyane’s rule at SARS tax dodging has become easier for the illicit industries costing the Revenue collector millions. The institution’s IT system and efiling system is facing collapse by year 2020 and a lot of skilled employees have been forced to leave the institution. Like many of the country’s institutions SARS’s mismanagement is detrimental to the state but it is more severe in this case as a huge chunk of treasury’s budget comes from tax and vat collection. However with all the findings from the commission will there be accountability more than just the culprit losing their job? How will SARS recover from this mess and what will it cost South Africans?

Carte Blanche will provide an overview of the Nugent commission and the preliminary report that came out of it and was send to the president for review. Testimonies and Visuals from the Nugent commission will be used to supplement the story along with interviews lined up from key players within the SARS debacle.

STRUCTURAL:
• SCRIPT “once a world class benchmark of tax collection efficiency has been brought to his knees”
• Say that Moyane is challenging his firing in the Constitutional Court
• Pauli’s intro can’t be that her expose’s led to NUGENT COMMISSION...reason given: http://www.thepresidency.gov.za/press-statements/president-ramaphosa-establishes-commission-inquiry-tax-administration-and
• Who was SARS investigating? Can you prove they were investigating ZUMA?
• In comes BAIN -- explain what they were supposed to do – restructure SARS HOW?
• RATHER LOSE LOXTON – his bites don’t take us forward
• Put in ROR of MAKWAKWA after section on him as COO
• Treatment is great!
• GARTNER’s deal with RANGEWAVE must be very clear – what

LEGAL:
• Streamline the story so that there’s no doubt about the allegation
• Is every fact & allegation confirmed & backed up by documents?
• Include ROR that Makwakwa says he is not aware of recommendations that he refused to implement...and served all commissioners; not compromised my integrity; always insisted that procurement processes be followed
• Struggled with the story -- a lot of allegations -- need to think about the way it’s set out -- difficult to understand what we’ve in
• Can we say that the losses are due to Moyane?
• BAIN -- had problems with tax; restructure SARS
• Allegation: Bain involved with Zuma...how do we know if was because of his own personal scrutiny and not genuinely
• Clarify what Bain got a contract for
• Put in Gartner’s response to allegation regarding Monyeki - “Gartner Consulting did not base its engagement with SARS on the word of Mr. Monyeki. After initial discussions with Mr. Monyeki in early December 2014, from late December 2014 through to the beginning of February 2015, there were protracted direct negotiations between Gartner Consulting and SARS (represented by Procurement and Legal) which were the basis for the initial IT Assessment. Mr. Monyeki was not involved in these discussions. These discussions were initiated by SARS, as detailed in Mr. Robinson’s statement.”
• Take out Loxton -- take our “YOU ARE STILL GUILTY OF THEFT”

Press Release:


SARS and the Nugent Commission
After years of political meddling and an inability to meet its revenue targets, President Cyril Ramaphosa established the Nugent Commission of Inquiry into tax administration and governance at SARS in May this year. With only a few weeks until its final report, due at the end of November, Carte Blanche examines the startling revelations that have emerged and whether SARS can be redeemed from the state of capture that defined it under suspended Commissioner Tom Moyane’s leadership.
Producer: Sophia Phirippides
Presenter: Derek Watts
Researchers: Siniketiwe Hlanze and Tony Beamish
Watch the trailer


Script:


VO: The South African Revenue Service, once a world class benchmark of efficient tax collection has been brought to its knees.// In an intricate web of intrigue and subterfuge, SARS and its people were plagued by controversy. //In a shock announcement this week, President Cyril Ramaphosa fired suspended Commissioner of SARS, Tom Moyane, on the recommendation of Judge Robert Nugent’s interim report of the SARs Inquiry.

NUGENT: As far as we are concerned the present commissioner should be removed as early as possible and a new commissioner put in.

LINK: The Nugent Commission was tasked with investigating, operational and corporate governance issues at SARS, while it was under the leadership of Commissioner Tom Moyane, who took the helm in September 2014.

VO: Judge Dennis Davis, of the Davis Tax Commission, is appalled at the current state of SARS and the effect it is having on the overall South African Economy.

Dennis: We know there was a decline in tax morality. as efficient as SARS as they had been previously was eroded. you could say 30, 40, 50 billion, each and every year just went down the toilet.

VO: Investigative journalist Pauli Van Wyk, has over the last four years unearthed corruption within SARS.

Pauli: One should never think that SARS was without problems. But when Tom Moyane came in, things started to change for the worse very quickly. It was not necessarily operational problems, as the previous Commissioners had. It was problems made and created by Tom Moyane.

VO: What led to such a harsh recommendation from Judge Nugent? Well, first we’ve got to go back a few years.

Link: In around 2012 ,2013, then president Jacob Zuma and his family found themselves with a few tax challenges. The best possible way for him to solve the problem, seemed to be to restructure SARS to be a little bit more understanding.

Pauli: Mr Zuma and his family and the Guptas and certain people propping up the ANC all were under scrutiny from SARS.

LINK: So how do you get the right man in the right place?

VO: In comes Bain & Company, an international consulting firm. Earmarks Tom Moyane as a candidate for the top job, and gets Mr Zuma’s buy in.

Pauli: Based on documents from Bain's own server, and obviously from our own investigations, that Bain first met with Mr Zuma, when he was still president in 2012, and they had this plan to overhaul the whole of government. In the running up to Mr Moyane being appointed as the head of SARS, he was briefed at least 6 times on how he would change SARS.

VO: Part of Bain’s business strategy was to secure government contracts. Evidence supporting Pauli Van Wyk’s assertion that Bain colluded with Tom Moyane and Jonas Makwakwa of SARS, as well as Zuma’s alleged fixer surfaced during her investigations. In an affidavit presented on behalf of Vittorio Massone, Bain’s former South African representative. Massone admitted that he met on eight occasions with Mr Moyane before he joined SARS.//

VO: In an email to Carte Blanche Jonas Makwakwa denies these allegations saying that he never allowed himself to be compromised by anyone throughout his years at SARS and he always respected processes and abided by them.

Pauli: Mr Moyane ensured that Bain received the contract. Bain charged around 187 million, including VAT.

VO:The contract awarded to Bain was to restructure SARS. During the Inquiry it was shown that, the tender application process only lasted 6 days … a deviation from procurement protocol.

Dennis: My understanding was they were brought in to advise the Commissioner as to an optimum structure for SARS at the time. I might add that we had been mandated by the Minister to look at issues relating to SARS.

VO: The restructuring of SARS, essentially ensured that key role players were either removed or kept in highly paid positions, but had little or no power.


Link: Amidst the collateral damage was the exit of COO Barry Hore, soon after Commissioner Moyane took the hot seat. Barry, was the architect of the modernisation process at SARS.

MS STEINBERG: So you're saying your modernisation programme was suspended before you'd had contact with him to explain what it was about, why you we redoing it?

MR HORE: That’s correct.

LINK: Every good general needs trusted lieutenants and for Tom Moyane, Jonas Makwakwa was his right hand man, who took over from Barry Hore as COO.

Pauli: Bain's idea and recommendations were that the Chief Operating Officer position, the position of Mr Barry Hore, was too powerful, and they tried to break it up. In the end, if you look at SARS, how it was in Mr Makwakwa's time, and Mr Moyane's time, they actually recreated the super-COO position and Mr Makwakwa was the Chief Operating Officer. So he, in effect, shunned Bain's advice, and he became very powerful, to the detriment of SARS

VO: In his response to us Mr Makwakwa states, “I’m not aware of any recommendations that I refused to implement and After completion of the work by BAIN and Gartner different people were assigned to implement the recommendations.”

Dennis: As I said to Judge Nugent when I gave evidence before him, our advice was in a sense to tweak that and to improve that which was part of an existing, incredibly efficient system.
Judge Davis: I’ll tell what the problems with Bain were is that I never quite understood what the entire need for this restructuring was, that actually SARS had a pretty good
mechanism,why do you need to fix something that’s not broke?

LINK: As with all forms of capture, friends always come in handy. Patrick Monyeki, apparently a close friend of commissioner Tom Moyane introduced Gartner an international IT consulting company to SARS through Neville Willemse, Gartner's senior management partner in South Africa, and a 200 million rand deal was struck, with very little to show for it.

Pauli: They only held the word of this middleman, Mr Patrick Monyeke, to start writing and to start working on a contract that they have not yet received and they had not spoken to SARS about.

VO: Advocate Steinberg asked Mr Neville Willemse, head of Gartner South Africa, if he knew that writing the terms of reference for a contract they had not yet received was illegal?

MS STEINBERG: Do you know in South African procurement law that that’s illegal?

MR WILLEMSE: My understanding is if it's

COMMISSIONER: Sorry. You must just answer the questions and the question was do you know that it was illegal?

MR WILLEMSE: No, I don’t know that.

MS STEINBERG: You don’t know?

MR WILLEMSE: No.

VO: In a written response to Carte Blanche, Gartner denies writing its own terms of reference. They say, “The document "RFP" was drafted by Mr. Monyeki. Mr. Willemse added comments to this document, which was then reviewed and amended by SARS”

VO: Judge Nugent questioned the ethics behind the awarding of the Gartner contract and brought International Gartner partner, Mike Lithgow to task.

COMMISSIONER: But the fact is that’s the evidence we heard this morning that Mr Monyeke spoke to Mr Willemse and said now this is what we’re going to do. This is what is coming from SARS. Gartner then settles terms of reference in consultation with Monyeke and has never spoke to the client at all. And by the way has no idea what Mr Monyeke’s relationship is with the client. Is that the kind of thing Gartner normally does in England for example?

MR LITHGOW: No, but I feel I’m being pushed into a corner here

VO: In their response to Carte Blanche, Gartner says they engaged with Procurement and Legal in “protracted direct negotiations” between them and SARS, “which were the basis for the initial IT assessment”


LINK: At some point rangewave got 40% of the deal, around 80 million rand.

VO: Gartner entered into a B-BBEE arrangement with Mr Monyeke’s company Rangewave for additional IT support.

LINK: Now rangewave Consulting tell us that Mr Monyeki is no longer a director or shareholder and that they have cut all ties with him...... mmm interesting we did try and contact him, but it appears he's not taking calls.

Pauli: Some of the IT structures, according to evidence under oath, is on the brink of collapse. Gartner and Bain would recommend certain features to be installed, but Mr Moyane and Mr Makwakwa would go on their own tangent and change the recommendations by their own

Dennis: We should be having a rather larger debate about, is the role of professional firms. and certainly consulting firms Their role in what has occured in the past decade in South Africa, their defence of what would clearly--a whole range of practices which essentially created a parallel state.

VO: And when it comes to the VAT increase this year, Judge Davis puts the blame squarely on SARS.

Dennis: Now consider this. If we had even been able to recoup 50% of the shortfall that we ran year-in and year-out in the three years that we alluded to, there would have been no need to have increased VAT by 1%. And that has had consequences on poor people.

VO: Tom Moyane is challenging his dismissal at the Constitutional Court having already refused to appear at the Commission. His Advocate Dali Mpofu, claimed double jeopardy, due to his simultaneous disciplinary hearing.

Dali Mpofu: The most unconstitutional thing since the dawn of democracy.

VO: Tom Moyane has not responded to Carte Blanche for an interview

Pauli:There's clear prima facie evidence that there was a lot of corruption involved These people must appear in court and they must explain to the country why they broke SARS.

Link: Acting commissioner of SARS Mark Kingon, has a tough road ahead of him and it's been difficult for him to witness the breakdown of the revenue service.

Dennis: I'm convinced that there are enough good people in SARS at present and I think there's enough good people outside SARS that could be brought back to as it were recover its former glory.

nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 08 November 2018 Press Release: SARS and the Nugent Commission After years of political meddling and an inability to meet its revenue targets, President Cyril Ramaphosa established the Nugent Commission of Inquiry into tax administration and governance at SARS in May this year. With only a few weeks until its final report, due at the end of November, Carte Blanche examines the startling revelations that have emerged and whether SARS can be redeemed from the state of capture that defined it under suspended Commissioner Tom Moyane’s leadership. Producer: Sophia Phirippides Presenter: Derek Watts Researchers: Siniketiwe Hlanze and Tony Beamish Watch the trailer Script: VO: The South African Revenue Service, once a world class benchmark of efficient tax collection has been brought to its knees.// In an intricate web of intrigue and subterfuge, SARS and its people were plagued by controversy. //In a shock announcement this week, President Cyril Ramaphosa fired suspended Commissioner of SARS, Tom Moyane, on the recommendation of Judge Robert Nugent’s interim report of the SARs Inquiry. NUGENT: As far as we are concerned the present commissioner should be removed as early as possible and a new commissioner put in. LINK: The Nugent Commission was tasked with investigating, operational and corporate governance issues at SARS, while it was under the leadership of Commissioner Tom Moyane, who took the helm in September 2014. VO: Judge Dennis Davis, of the Davis Tax Commission, is appalled at the current state of SARS and the effect it is having on the overall South African Economy. Dennis: We know there was a decline in tax morality. as efficient as SARS as they had been previously was eroded. you could say 30, 40, 50 billion, each and every year just went down the toilet. VO: Investigative journalist Pauli Van Wyk, has over the last four years unearthed corruption within SARS. Pauli: One should never think that SARS was without problems. But when Tom Moyane came in, things started to change for the worse very quickly. It was not necessarily operational problems, as the previous Commissioners had. It was problems made and created by Tom Moyane. VO: What led to such a harsh recommendation from Judge Nugent? Well, first we’ve got to go back a few years. Link: In around 2012 ,2013, then president Jacob Zuma and his family found themselves with a few tax challenges. The best possible way for him to solve the problem, seemed to be to restructure SARS to be a little bit more understanding. Pauli: Mr Zuma and his family and the Guptas and certain people propping up the ANC all were under scrutiny from SARS. LINK: So how do you get the right man in the right place? VO: In comes Bain & Company, an international consulting firm. Earmarks Tom Moyane as a candidate for the top job, and gets Mr Zuma’s buy in. Pauli: Based on documents from Bain's own server, and obviously from our own investigations, that Bain first met with Mr Zuma, when he was still president in 2012, and they had this plan to overhaul the whole of government. In the running up to Mr Moyane being appointed as the head of SARS, he was briefed at least 6 times on how he would change SARS. VO: Part of Bain’s business strategy was to secure government contracts. Evidence supporting Pauli Van Wyk’s assertion that Bain colluded with Tom Moyane and Jonas Makwakwa of SARS, as well as Zuma’s alleged fixer surfaced during her investigations. In an affidavit presented on behalf of Vittorio Massone, Bain’s former South African representative. Massone admitted that he met on eight occasions with Mr Moyane before he joined SARS.// VO: In an email to Carte Blanche Jonas Makwakwa denies these allegations saying that he never allowed himself to be compromised by anyone throughout his years at SARS and he always respected processes and abided by them. Pauli: Mr Moyane ensured that Bain received the contract. Bain charged around 187 million, including VAT. VO:The contract awarded to Bain was to restructure SARS. During the Inquiry it was shown that, the tender application process only lasted 6 days … a deviation from procurement protocol. Dennis: My understanding was they were brought in to advise the Commissioner as to an optimum structure for SARS at the time. I might add that we had been mandated by the Minister to look at issues relating to SARS. VO: The restructuring of SARS, essentially ensured that key role players were either removed or kept in highly paid positions, but had little or no power. Link: Amidst the collateral damage was the exit of COO Barry Hore, soon after Commissioner Moyane took the hot seat. Barry, was the architect of the modernisation process at SARS. MS STEINBERG: So you're saying your modernisation programme was suspended before you'd had contact with him to explain what it was about, why you we redoing it? MR HORE: That’s correct. LINK: Every good general needs trusted lieutenants and for Tom Moyane, Jonas Makwakwa was his right hand man, who took over from Barry Hore as COO. Pauli: Bain's idea and recommendations were that the Chief Operating Officer position, the position of Mr Barry Hore, was too powerful, and they tried to break it up. In the end, if you look at SARS, how it was in Mr Makwakwa's time, and Mr Moyane's time, they actually recreated the super-COO position and Mr Makwakwa was the Chief Operating Officer. So he, in effect, shunned Bain's advice, and he became very powerful, to the detriment of SARS VO: In his response to us Mr Makwakwa states, “I’m not aware of any recommendations that I refused to implement and After completion of the work by BAIN and Gartner different people were assigned to implement the recommendations.” Dennis: As I said to Judge Nugent when I gave evidence before him, our advice was in a sense to tweak that and to improve that which was part of an existing, incredibly efficient system. Judge Davis: I’ll tell what the problems with Bain were is that I never quite understood what the entire need for this restructuring was, that actually SARS had a pretty good mechanism,why do you need to fix something that’s not broke? LINK: As with all forms of capture, friends always come in handy. Patrick Monyeki, apparently a close friend of commissioner Tom Moyane introduced Gartner an international IT consulting company to SARS through Neville Willemse, Gartner's senior management partner in South Africa, and a 200 million rand deal was struck, with very little to show for it. Pauli: They only held the word of this middleman, Mr Patrick Monyeke, to start writing and to start working on a contract that they have not yet received and they had not spoken to SARS about. VO: Advocate Steinberg asked Mr Neville Willemse, head of Gartner South Africa, if he knew that writing the terms of reference for a contract they had not yet received was illegal? MS STEINBERG: Do you know in South African procurement law that that’s illegal? MR WILLEMSE: My understanding is if it's COMMISSIONER: Sorry. You must just answer the questions and the question was do you know that it was illegal? MR WILLEMSE: No, I don’t know that. MS STEINBERG: You don’t know? MR WILLEMSE: No. VO: In a written response to Carte Blanche, Gartner denies writing its own terms of reference. They say, “The document "RFP" was drafted by Mr. Monyeki. Mr. Willemse added comments to this document, which was then reviewed and amended by SARS” VO: Judge Nugent questioned the ethics behind the awarding of the Gartner contract and brought International Gartner partner, Mike Lithgow to task. COMMISSIONER: But the fact is that’s the evidence we heard this morning that Mr Monyeke spoke to Mr Willemse and said now this is what we’re going to do. This is what is coming from SARS. Gartner then settles terms of reference in consultation with Monyeke and has never spoke to the client at all. And by the way has no idea what Mr Monyeke’s relationship is with the client. Is that the kind of thing Gartner normally does in England for example? MR LITHGOW: No, but I feel I’m being pushed into a corner here VO: In their response to Carte Blanche, Gartner says they engaged with Procurement and Legal in “protracted direct negotiations” between them and SARS, “which were the basis for the initial IT assessment” LINK: At some point rangewave got 40% of the deal, around 80 million rand. VO: Gartner entered into a B-BBEE arrangement with Mr Monyeke’s company Rangewave for additional IT support. LINK: Now rangewave Consulting tell us that Mr Monyeki is no longer a director or shareholder and that they have cut all ties with him...... mmm interesting we did try and contact him, but it appears he's not taking calls. Pauli: Some of the IT structures, according to evidence under oath, is on the brink of collapse. Gartner and Bain would recommend certain features to be installed, but Mr Moyane and Mr Makwakwa would go on their own tangent and change the recommendations by their own Dennis: We should be having a rather larger debate about, is the role of professional firms. and certainly consulting firms Their role in what has occured in the past decade in South Africa, their defence of what would clearly--a whole range of practices which essentially created a parallel state. VO: And when it comes to the VAT increase this year, Judge Davis puts the blame squarely on SARS. Dennis: Now consider this. If we had even been able to recoup 50% of the shortfall that we ran year-in and year-out in the three years that we alluded to, there would have been no need to have increased VAT by 1%. And that has had consequences on poor people. VO: Tom Moyane is challenging his dismissal at the Constitutional Court having already refused to appear at the Commission. His Advocate Dali Mpofu, claimed double jeopardy, due to his simultaneous disciplinary hearing. Dali Mpofu: The most unconstitutional thing since the dawn of democracy. VO: Tom Moyane has not responded to Carte Blanche for an interview Pauli:There's clear prima facie evidence that there was a lot of corruption involved These people must appear in court and they must explain to the country why they broke SARS. Link: Acting commissioner of SARS Mark Kingon, has a tough road ahead of him and it's been difficult for him to witness the breakdown of the revenue service. Dennis: I'm convinced that there are enough good people in SARS at present and I think there's enough good people outside SARS that could be brought back to as it were recover its former glory.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): SARS has been marred by allegations of corruption and staff exodus recently. Failing to meet its tax collection targets for 3 consecutive years, how will a crippled tax institution impact the taxpayer
metadata.Unique Selling Point: The South African Revenue service is a pivotal institution to the stability of the country. In the past few years as with many other state institutions, SARS has been in the media for all the wrong reasons. From allegations of rogue units to the failure to meet its tax collection targets three years in a row with some of its staff members testifying at the Nugent commission that SARS’ shortfalls are also key to the increase of VAT. How did an institution that is so integral to the welfare of the country get so crippled?
metadata.Summary: When a government institution fails to achieve its core mandate as such with SARS it is a cause for concern. SARS’ main objective is to collect tax revenue for the state, which they have failed to do efficiently for the past three years. The troubles at SARS began with the appointment of Mr Tom Moyane who became SARS commissioner on the 27th of September 2014. Under Mr Moyane’s stewardship the institution has regressed with allegations of corruption, procurement irregularities and staff intimidation from the commissioner himself and his enforcers. This prompted President Cyril Ramaphosa to initiate a commission looking into SARS led by former Judge, Robert Nugent, dubbed the Nugent Commission.
metadata.Further information: Startling testimonies have come out of the commission since it began its work in May 2018 following the suspension of Tom Moyane. For starters a consulting firm, Bain & Company in 2014 conducted a diagnostic for the South African Revenue Service that formed the basis for the overhauling process at the institution and kick-started an entire restructuring process. To many, the restructuring came as a surprise. It resulted in the closure of crucial arms such as the unit investigating the illicit economy, which chased down the illegal tobacco trade among others, and the Large Business Centre that made sure large enterprises paid their tax dues. Although Bain & company has pledged to pay back the R164 million they made from SARS for services rendered, the R50b revenue shortfall they have cost SARS in the 2017/18 financial year will take a few years for the institution to recover. The Nugent commission has also revealed that suspended commissioner Tom Moyane also got involved in dubious appointment of these companies. It appears Moyane met with Bain & co.’s management partner Vittorio Massone at least a year prior to even becoming a commissioner. Massone testified that he had met with Moyane who asked for work to be done on SARS while he was still commissioner of the department correctional services, a clear indication that the two had a relationship before Bain & co got awarded the tender that was only advertised unusually for six days. Moyane’s iron rule in the institution was not only dominant in the fear entrenched within the SARS staff members who testified at the commission, but his management of SARS also reeked of corruption, similar to that shown in state capture and other state entities. The appointment of Global advisory firm Gartner and Range wave to have an IT review into SARS was also quite dodgy and had Moyane’s finger prints on it. Patrick Monyeki of Range wave is known to be a close friend of Tom Moyane and he was the one who brought the deal in December 2014 to Gartner, according to the firm’s senior management partner Neville Willemse. Monyeki’s company received 40%, about R80m fro Gartner’s R200m contract with Sars. Gartener however belives they were not given enough to refute al these allegations by the Nugent commission. They do not know anything about transactions between Patrick Monyeki and SARS or how Gartner was chosen for the contract. According to them, they did not temper with the terms of reference of the job but merely commented on it, which in itself its not illegal, particularly if it will help save costs. An aggrieved Gartner are disappointed by the blame they have received for the collapse of SARS while none of their recommendations were used by SARS. Judge Dennis Davies who heads up the Davis Tax Committee testified at the Nugent commission that he never saw the need for restructuring at SARS. "Why fix what is to broken" was his comments. Davis was appointed by then finance minister Pravin Gordhan in 2014 to update the process of the Katz commission but instead Commissioner Moyane saw the Davis Tax committee as an enemy. As a result the commission wasn't given access to key data. Furthermore Davis said the recommendations in the Bain report were diametrically opposite to their advice. There were disastrous consequences because of the Large Business Centre Collapse, all kinds of problems in corporate taxes as a result. David Loxton of Africa forensics and cyber believes that although Judge Nugent has recommended in his report that the President must fire Mr Moyane and appoint a new commissioner, there should be legal repercussions to Mr Moyane and his enforcers at SARS. Corruption is a crime and so those involved must account to the law. David believes there was a concerted effort by Moyane and those close to him to undo all the good within SARS and cripple the institution. This was a corporate strategy to put taxpayer’s monies in risk. Under Moyane’s rule at SARS tax dodging has become easier for the illicit industries costing the Revenue collector millions. The institution’s IT system and efiling system is facing collapse by year 2020 and a lot of skilled employees have been forced to leave the institution. Like many of the country’s institutions SARS’s mismanagement is detrimental to the state but it is more severe in this case as a huge chunk of treasury’s budget comes from tax and vat collection. However with all the findings from the commission will there be accountability more than just the culprit losing their job? How will SARS recover from this mess and what will it cost South Africans? Carte Blanche will provide an overview of the Nugent commission and the preliminary report that came out of it and was send to the president for review. Testimonies and Visuals from the Nugent commission will be used to supplement the story along with interviews lined up from key players within the SARS debacle.
